newsitem.title: DUBAI: Bahrain threatens to boycott Gulf Arab summit.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain threatens to boycott Gulf Arab summit.

text.p: Bahrain threatened on Sunday to boycott a summit of Gulf Arab leaders due to be held in Qatar in December if Qatar did not withdraw a case it had taken to the World Court over its territorial dispute with Bahrain.

Diplomats in Saudi Arabia said Bahrain made the threat in in a letter delivered on Sunday to the Riyadh-based general secretariat of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) which also groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, and United Arab Emirates.

A statement by the Bahraini embassy in Riyadh said the letter "pointed out that it is not possible, rather it is difficult (for Bahrain) to take part in a summit held in brotherly Qatar which has lodged a legal case...against Bahrain at the International Court of Justice."
It said "among the reasons that prompt Bahrain not to take part in the summit" are concerns that Qatar would insist that the territorial row with Bahrian be discussed at the summit.
Leaders of the oil-rich Gulf Arab states hold a summit every year in December in a different member state. It is due to be held in Qatar this year.
Bahrain and Qatar are locked in a long-standing row over a number of barren but potentially oil and gas-rich Gulf islands, sandbanks and reefs controlled by Bahrain since the mid-1930s.

Qatar unilaterally asked the World Court in 1991 to settle the problem, but Bahrain has rejected the jurisdiction of the court, which decided in January that it had jurisdiction and is expected to produce a ruling this year.
Bahrain has repeatedly urged Qatar to withdraw the case and accept Saudi arbitration. Qatar said it would only withdraw the case if Saudi Arabian mediation succeeded.
